---
title: "Quiz: Paired measurements"
---

[Exercises](18-paired.qmd) · [Lecture slides](../lectures/18-paired/lec.qmd)

Try each question before opening its hint or answer.

---

**Q1.** Plants D1, D2, D3 have before readings 5, 8, 6 and after readings 7, 9, 9
in the same order, in µmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Calculate their changes and mean change.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Subtract before from after for each matching identifier.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Changes are **2, 1, 3**; mean change is **2 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹**. These are
three independent pairs, not six independent plants.
:::

---

**Q2.** Which function call estimates after minus before for matched plants?

(i) `t.test(after, before, paired = TRUE)`  

(ii) `t.test(before, after, paired = TRUE)`  

(iii) `t.test(after, before, paired = FALSE)`

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Both the pairing argument and vector order matter.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
(i). (ii) estimates the reverse direction; (iii) treats the two vectors as
independent groups.
:::

---

**Q3.** Independently sorting the before and after columns preserves their
means. Does that make the resulting paired test valid?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
Pairing carries subject identity, which is more information than two means.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
No. Sorting columns separately destroys the original plant matching. The
mean difference can remain unchanged while the SD of within-plant changes and
the confidence interval change. Move complete rows together.
:::

---

**Q4.** A 95% interval for mean change is [−0.48, 4.48] in the stated rate units.
Does it prove no change, or contain 95% of individual changes?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
The interval describes uncertainty in a mean change under the assumptions.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Neither. It spans zero and both positive and negative mean changes; the
small dataset does not resolve direction at this interval level. It is not an
individual-change range or proof of equivalence.
:::

---

**Q5.** All plants are measured before, then after changing light. A paired
test gives a small p-value. Why is light alone still not established as the cause?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Hint"}
What else changes between the first and second reading?
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer"}
Elapsed time, acclimation, measurement order, or equipment drift may
contribute. The test addresses mean change; a suitable comparison and design
addressing order effects are needed to isolate causes.
:::
